1.subtopic: Direct a Friend Around a Maze
1.outline: Term theme: 'Play, Code & Be Awesome'. Give step-by-step instructions to direct a partner around a taped-floor maze, learning that a computer program is just a sequence of steps.
objectives: Give clear step-by-step instructions.
Follow a partner's instructions exactly.
Explain that a program is a sequence of steps.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a sequence?
plan.detail: Explain: a sequence is steps done in order. Everyday example: getting dressed.

plan.title: Maze game
plan.detail: In pairs, one gives instructions (forward, turn left/right) to direct the other around a taped maze.

plan.title: Reflect
plan.detail: What happened when an instruction was unclear? Log out.

successCriteria: I gave clear instructions to a partner.
I followed instructions exactly.
I can say that a program is a sequence of steps.

2.subtopic: Make a Character Move Across the Screen
2.outline: Open ScratchJr and use motion blocks to make a character move from one side of the screen to the other.
objectives: Open ScratchJr and choose a character.
Use motion blocks to move the character.
Test the program by tapping the green flag.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: ScratchJr tour
plan.detail: Show the character, the block palette and the green flag start button.

plan.title: Make it move
plan.detail: Drag motion blocks to make the character move across the screen; test with the flag.

plan.title: Show a partner
plan.detail: Show a partner the character moving. Log out.

successCriteria: I opened ScratchJr and chose a character.
My character moves when I tap the flag.
I can show a partner my working program.

3.subtopic: Add a Sound and a Second Movement
3.outline: Extend the moving character with a sound block and a second movement, building a slightly longer sequence.
objectives: Add a sound block to the program.
Add a second movement block.
Explain the order the blocks run in.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add a sound
plan.detail: Add a sound block after the movement and test it.

plan.title: Add a second move
plan.detail: Add a second movement block after the sound, so the sequence gets longer.

plan.title: Explain the order
plan.detail: Explain to a partner what happens first, second, third. Log out.

successCriteria: My program has a sound block.
My program has two movement blocks.
I can explain the order my blocks run in.

4.subtopic: Find and Fix the Wrong Step
4.outline: Given a ScratchJr program that doesn't do what it should, find the wrong block and fix it — first experience of debugging.
objectives: Watch a broken program and spot what's wrong.
Fix the broken block or order.
Explain what 'debugging' means.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a bug?
plan.detail: A bug is something that makes the program not work as expected. Show a simple example.

plan.title: Fix three programs
plan.detail: Open three pre-made broken ScratchJr projects and fix each one.

plan.title: Share a fix
plan.detail: Share which bug was trickiest to spot. Log out.

successCriteria: I can explain what a bug is.
I fixed at least two broken programs.
I can say what 'debugging' means.

5.outline: Play Google Interland's 'Kind Kingdom' to practise being kind and respectful, even in a game or online space.
objectives: Play Kind Kingdom and make kind choices.
Explain what being kind online looks like.
Explain what to do if someone is unkind.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Kind Kingdom
plan.detail: Play the Interland game, discussing the choices as they come up.

plan.title: Kindness examples
plan.detail: As a class, list examples of being kind online.

plan.title: What to do
plan.detail: Discuss: if someone is unkind, tell a trusted adult. Log out.

successCriteria: I played Kind Kingdom and made kind choices.
I can give one example of being kind online.
I know to tell a trusted adult about unkindness.

6.outline: Play Google Interland's 'Mindful Mountain' to practise thinking before sharing, and revisit what stays private.
objectives: Play Mindful Mountain and practise thinking before sharing.
Name one thing that should stay private.
Explain why thinking before sharing matters.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Mindful Mountain
plan.detail: Play the Interland game, discussing the sharing decisions as they come up.

plan.title: Private things recap
plan.detail: Recap private things from earlier terms: name, address, photos.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Each pupil names one private thing. Log out.

successCriteria: I played Mindful Mountain and thought before sharing.
I can name one thing that should stay private.
I can explain why thinking before sharing matters.

7.subtopic: A Character That Waves and Says Hello
7.outline: Build a short animation of a character that waves and 'says' hello, using motion and sound blocks together.
objectives: Plan a simple wave-and-hello animation.
Build it using motion and sound blocks.
Test and improve it.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Plan it
plan.detail: Sketch what the character will do: wave, then a hello sound.

plan.title: Build and test
plan.detail: Build the animation, test it, and improve the timing if needed.

plan.title: Show a partner
plan.detail: Show a partner the finished animation. Log out.

successCriteria: I planned my wave-and-hello animation.
My animation uses motion and sound blocks.
I tested and improved my animation.

8.subtopic: Share Animations; One Kind Comment Each
8.outline: Share the finished hello animations with the class and give one kind, specific comment to a classmate.
objectives: Share a finished animation with the class.
Give one kind, specific comment.
Save the finished animation.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Showcase
plan.detail: Small groups take turns sharing their animation on a shared screen.

plan.title: Kind comments
plan.detail: Each pupil gives one kind, specific comment to a classmate.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save the animation to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: I shared my animation with the class.
I gave one kind, specific comment.
My animation is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Recap this term's skills: sequences, movement, sound and simple debugging, through a quick station rotation.
objectives: Recap sequences, movement, sound and debugging.
Complete each station task.
Identify which skill needs more practice.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Station 1 — Sequence
plan.detail: Give and follow a short instruction sequence.

plan.title: Station 2 — Build
plan.detail: Add a movement and sound block to a starter project.

plan.title: Station 3 — Debug
plan.detail: Fix one small bug in a project.

plan.title: Reflect
plan.detail: Name the skill you found trickiest. Log out.

successCriteria: I completed all three stations.
I can recap sequences, movement, sound and debugging.
I know which skill needs more practice.

10.outline: Rehearse the practical task in pairs: build a short animation with movement, sound and no bugs left in it.
objectives: Rehearse building a short animation with a partner.
Check it for bugs before finishing.
Explain what the animation does.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build a short animation with a partner, checking each other's work for bugs.

plan.title: Explain it
plan.detail: Explain the finished animation to the partner. Log out.

successCriteria: I rehearsed building a short animation with a partner.
I checked for and fixed any bugs.
I explained what my animation does.

11.outline: Individual task: build a short ScratchJr animation using at least a movement and a sound block, then explain what it does.
objectives: Build a short animation independently.
Use a movement block and a sound block.
Explain what my animation does.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — this is a 'show me what you can do' task.

plan.title: Group A practical
plan.detail: First group builds the animation while others do independent TypingClub.

plan.title: Group B practical
plan.detail: Second group, same task.

plan.title: Explain and celebrate
plan.detail: One-to-one: explain the animation. Celebrate the year's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: I built an animation using a movement block.
My animation includes a sound block.
I explained what my animation does.

12.outline: Plan a final project: a friendly robot character that moves, makes a sound, and shares one kind message.
objectives: Plan a robot character and its actions.
Decide on the kind message it will share.
Sketch the plan on paper.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Plan the robot
plan.detail: Sketch the robot, its movement, its sound, and its kind message on the planning sheet.

plan.title: Pitch it
plan.detail: Tell a partner the plan. Collect plans. Log out.

successCriteria: My plan shows the robot's movement.
My plan includes a kind message.
I can tell a partner my plan.

13.outline: Build the Kind Robot animation in ScratchJr, following the plan: movement, sound, and the kind message.
objectives: Build the robot's movement.
Add the sound and kind message.
Test the finished animation.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the robot
plan.detail: Follow the plan to build movement, sound and the kind message blocks.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Test the whole sequence and fix anything that doesn't work. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My robot moves as planned.
My robot shares its kind message.
I tested my animation and fixed any bugs.

14.outline: Add one polish touch to the Kind Robot — an extra sound, a second character, or a background — and rehearse presenting it.
objectives: Add one polish feature to the animation.
Rehearse presenting the animation.
Save the finished project.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add polish
plan.detail: Add a background, extra sound or second character.

plan.title: Rehearse
plan.detail: Practise presenting the animation to a partner.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save the finished project. Log out.

successCriteria: My animation has one polish feature.
I rehearsed presenting it to a partner.
My finished project is saved.

15.outline: Present the finished Kind Robot to the class or a younger class, sharing the kind message, and save the year's portfolio.
objectives: Present the finished animation confidently.
Share the robot's kind message with an audience.
Save the whole year's portfolio.

plan.title: Final rehearsal
plan.detail: One last run-through with a partner before presenting.

plan.title: Kind Robot Fair
plan.detail: Present animations to the class or visitors in small groups.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save the finished project and look back at the whole year's portfolio folder.

plan.title: Year celebration
plan.detail: Name three things learned this year. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my Kind Robot confidently.
I shared its kind message with an audience.
My whole year's work is saved in the portfolio.
